issues.description: findHue has no written contract for how 'from <origin>' prefix interacts with the channel triple
issues.detail: All three reviewers flag that the function's precondition on node shape and postcondition on which arg is the hue are implicit. The bug existed because the contract conflated 'hue is at index 0 or 2' with 'hue is at index 0 or 2 of the channel list excluding the from-origin prefix.' State the contract in a comment so future relative-color variants don't regress.

issues.description: Test fixtures declare fix.text as '0deg' where the inserted string should be 'deg'
issues.detail: Two reject cases set fix.text to '0deg' over a 1-char range that only spans the position after the number (e.g. '10' becoming '10deg'). The replacement should be 'deg'. Either the harness silently ignores fix.text or the payload is wrong. Verify and correct the fixtures so the assertions actually prove the fixer's output.

issues.description: Relative-color detection by args[0].value === 'from' is a structural heuristic, not a parse
issues.detail: Both Dijkstra and Liskov note that recognising relative-color form by lowercased value of the first word token conflates the CSS keyword with any identifier reading 'from'. The invariant holds in CSS Color 5 today but is asserted, not proved. Add a comment citing the grammar, or cross-check against function name plus arg count, to document the precondition.

issues.description: Magic '0 + offset' and '2 + offset' obscure the algorithm; name the hue index
issues.detail: Both Dijkstra and Pike call out args[0 + offset] and args[2 + offset] as cosmetic noise. Prefer args[offset] and args[offset + 2], or better, a named hueIndex constant derived from the function-name lookup table. Small change, makes the algorithm read itself.

issues.description: Missing test coverage for nested relative color where the outer hue also needs fixing
issues.detail: All three reviewers want a reject case where both the outer function's hue is wrong AND the inner function is itself a relative color or has a fixable hue. The current accept-only nested case doesn't lock in that args[0] lookup isn't fooled by a function-typed first arg or by recursive relative forms.

issues.description: Args array conflates from-prefix and channel triple; extract a small helper returning channels
issues.detail: Liskov and Pike both want the right abstraction: either a ParsedColorFunction with explicit {origin, channels} fields, or a tiny lookup table {funcName: hueIndex} plus relativeOffset(args). Removes the index gymnastics and makes future channel-prefixed syntaxes substitutable rather than requiring another offset hack.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the fix is small, local, and correct in shape — detect 'from' as the first arg and shift the hue index by 2 — but it ships as a point fix rather than a properly abstracted change. The chief deficiency is unstated contract: findHue has no written pre/postcondition, and the patch papers over the from-prefix vs channel-triple distinction with an offset constant. Test fixtures also contain a suspicious fix.text='0deg' that looks like a copy-paste artifact and warrants verification. Naming the hue index, documenting the relative-color invariant, and adding a nested-fix test case would lift this from tested-not-proved to reasoned code.
